correctness.rationale: With one raw variable the only nouns are \(p\) and its complement. Evaluating all four sentence forms shows that every nontrivial sentence is one of eight conditions on \(k=|p|\): \(k=0,k=n,k>0,k<n,2k\ge n,2k\le n,2k>n,2k<n\). Any consistent theory is therefore equivalent to one strongest lower bound from \(0,1,\lceil n/2\rceil,\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1,n\) and one strongest upper bound from \(n,n-1,\lfloor n/2\rfloor,\lceil n/2\rceil-1,0\). Exact comparison of the 25 pairs yields only the five stated spectra. I independently enumerated all 256 subsets of the eight semantic constraints through universe size 80 and obtained exactly those five patterns; this finite replay corroborates, rather than replaces, the symbolic reduction. The frozen verifier was read in full.
correctness.risk: Only the one-variable fragment is classified; nothing here determines the exact two-variable hierarchy.

value.rationale: The result is the natural base case of a vocabulary-resource hierarchy left implicit by the unrestricted theorem. It sharply separates two expressive mechanisms: parity survives with one raw variable, while lower-bound expressivity stops at three. Natural complete fragment classifications qualify under the common value bar even when the final table is small.

final_claim: In the original non-Boolean one-raw-variable fragment of \(S^\dagger(card)\), every finite spectrum is exactly one of \(\varnothing,T_1,T_2,T_3,E_2\), and all five occur.
